chapters.title: External provider lab: boundaries
paragraphs: These artifacts create actual provider resources only after operator authorization. No live provider deployment was performed.
Connected platforms synchronizes inventory. It does not deploy external agents into Teams or establish runtime telemetry. [V01]
ONB-10, actual Bedrock registry synchronization, is REQUIRED for the requested connected-platform category, despite preview status.
Provider readiness, ONB-05, does not satisfy ONB-10. Record the actual synchronized registry entry and matching provider AgentId.
ONB-07, actual Claude Managed Agents registry synchronization, is also REQUIRED. Missing beta or preview approval blocks agreed catalogue acceptance.
Use isolated test accounts, synthetic content, approved regions, and customer-approved spending limits.

sections.title: Files and local validation
paragraphs: The AWS template creates one Bedrock Agent and one service role. It creates no access keys.
The Anthropic script uses Python standard-library HTTPS. No provider package installation is required.
Tests replace provider transports. They never authenticate or contact customer accounts.

Run the standard unittest suite.
Review the provider-specific eligibility gates before live testing.

chapters.title: Amazon Bedrock: create an isolated inventory agent
paragraphs: This template targets AWS::Bedrock::Agent, now called Bedrock Agents Classic. It does not create an AgentCore runtime. [V02, V05]
Agents Classic closed to new customers on July 30, 2026. Existing Agents Classic customers can continue using it. [V05]
For new Agents Classic customers, mark this Classic path BLOCKED. An existing AWS account alone does not establish eligibility.
Do not silently substitute AgentCore. A separate AgentCore demonstration requires a separately scoped plan and explicit customer approval.

sections.title: Model, role, and cost gates
paragraphs: Select an approved, available direct foundation model in the approved region. No model availability is assumed. [V04]
The script accepts a provider-qualified model ID or its same-region foundation-model ARN. It rejects profile ARNs and us., eu., apac., and global. routing prefixes.
Inference profiles require additional actions and resource scoping. This deliberately narrow template does not grant those permissions. [V03]
Bedrock inference can incur charges. The script prepares the agent but never invokes it.
steps: Confirm existing Agents Classic customer eligibility with the AWS account owner. Otherwise mark the Classic path BLOCKED.
Confirm the chosen model, regional availability, quotas, model access, pricing, and purchasing terms.
Use an already approved AWS CLI v2 session. This script does not sign in or switch accounts.
Confirm the active principal can manage this stack, create its role, and pass that role to Bedrock.
items: The service role permits only bedrock:InvokeModel on one foundation-model ARN.
Trust permits bedrock.amazonaws.com, constrained by the current account and region.
Bootstrap trust uses agent/*. A second reviewed update pins the returned AgentId.
The role has no S3, Lambda, knowledge-base, credential, or connector permissions.
The agent has no action groups, knowledge bases, external tools, or collaborators.
notes: Do not confuse the agent service role with operator permissions or Microsoft connector credentials.
The customer must approve each permission set separately.
The model policy and trust conditions follow AWS documentation. [V03]

sections.title: Preview, prepare, review, and execute
paragraphs: Replace every uppercase value before running the commands.
Use the same exact stack name throughout the lab. The example name is a365-bedrock-lab.
The normal command creates a change set, not deployed resources. This is still an authenticated AWS control-plane write. [V06]
WhatIf is fully local. It does not read credentials or call AWS.
steps: Run the WhatIf command first.
Remove WhatIf to prepare a change set. Confirm the preparation prompt.
Record its ChangeSetId. Inspect all changes, model parameters, IAM policy, tags, account, and region.
Use -Apply -Confirm with that exact ChangeSetId. Confirm the execution prompt.
Wait for a completed stack. Record AgentId, account, region, and stack name.
Prepare a second change set using the same creation parameters.
The second update automatically pins role trust to the existing AgentId. Review and execute that update separately.
items: The script refuses account or approved-region mismatches.
Execution requires explicit -Confirm, including execution previews. Omitted confirmation and -Confirm:$false are rejected before AWS calls, regardless of the caller's ConfirmPreference.
It checks demo ownership tags before updating an existing deployed stack.
It does not treat access-denied errors as a missing stack.
Failed or incomplete change sets are never executed.
An empty change set reports no changes, not a successful deployment.
Failed stack waiters do not produce a successful AgentId result.
sections.code:
$common = @{
  StackName = 'a365-bedrock-lab'
  ExpectedAccountId = 'APPROVED_12_DIGIT_ACCOUNT'
  Region = 'APPROVED_REGION'
  ApprovedRegion = 'APPROVED_REGION'
  ConfirmClassicAccess = $true
}
$create = @{
  AgentName = 'a365-bedrock-lab'
  FoundationModel = 'APPROVED_DIRECT_MODEL_ID_OR_ARN'
  Owner = 'lab-team'
}
.\providers\aws\Prepare-BedrockDemo.ps1 @common @create -WhatIf
# After approval: prepare only.
.\providers\aws\Prepare-BedrockDemo.ps1 @common @create -Confirm
# After reviewing the returned change set:
.\providers\aws\Prepare-BedrockDemo.ps1 @common -Apply -Confirm -ChangeSetId 'RETURNED_CHANGE_SET_ARN'
# After CREATE_COMPLETE: prepare the exact-AgentId trust update.
.\providers\aws\Prepare-BedrockDemo.ps1 @common @create -Confirm
# Review this new change set before execution.
.\providers\aws\Prepare-BedrockDemo.ps1 @common -Apply -Confirm -ChangeSetId 'RETURNED_TRUST_UPDATE_CHANGE_SET_ARN'
notes: An unexecuted CREATE change set can leave an empty REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS stack.
A failed change set remains available for investigation and exact-ID removal.
Do not retry after an uncertain timeout without inspecting the exact stack and change set.
AWS calls use 15-second connection and 30-second read timeouts. AWS CLI waiters have finite retry limits.
AWS error output is suppressed. Inspect the exact stack or change set in the approved AWS interface.
DescribeChangeSet does not return ChangeSetType. The script uses its preparation marker and verified stack state. [V07]
Changes to AWS or model access can still fail during execution. Local validation is not a deployment guarantee.

sections.title: Hand off for manual Microsoft connection
paragraphs: Use the printed AgentId to verify the inventory entry after manual synchronization.
ONB-10 is REQUIRED. A created provider agent without actual registry synchronization does not pass the connected-platform demonstration.
The Microsoft wizard needs separate customer-approved AWS credentials and the deployment region. [V01]
This template does not create, retrieve, print, store, or rotate those credentials.
Microsoft's documented permission list includes invocation and deletion. Do not describe this connector as read-only. [V01]
steps: Obtain separate customer approval for the documented connector permission list.
Have the authorized administrator enter credentials directly in the Microsoft wizard.
Use the platform onboarding chapter for the portal connection and synchronization procedure.
Perform the actual Bedrock registry synchronization. Compare the synchronized provider AgentId with the stack output.
Record connection identity, account, region, synchronization status, timestamp, registry entry, and matching AgentId as ONB-10 evidence.
Mark ONB-10 BLOCKED if eligibility, permissions, or preview availability prevents synchronization. Do not report provider readiness as PASS.

sections.title: Remove only the approved lab stack
paragraphs: Cleanup is optional and destructive. Obtain approval before deleting the exact lab stack.
Stop if the account, region, stack name, or ownership tags differ.
Do not delete stacks by prefix or enumerate stacks for deletion.
steps: Remove the Microsoft platform connection through the documented manual procedure.
Have the credential owner revoke the dedicated connector credentials.
Run the guarded cleanup below with the same approved account and region.
Inspect DELETE_FAILED stack events instead of disabling resource-in-use protections.
notes: An empty REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS stack may lack tags. Inspect its exact change set manually before deleting it.
Use the AWS console for that exceptional cleanup. Do not remove the ownership checks from this snippet.
Stack deletion does not revoke separately created Microsoft connector credentials.

chapters.title: Anthropic Claude Managed Agents beta: synthetic agent
paragraphs: This implementation calls documented Anthropic APIs. It does not use the Messages API as a substitute for Managed Agents. [V08]
Managed Agents is stateful. It is not currently eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA BAA coverage. [V09]
Approve that data-handling boundary before using this beta. Use synthetic arithmetic only.

sections.title: Workspace and network gates
paragraphs: Use a new non-default workspace. Microsoft requires its workspace ID and a workspace-scoped API key. [V01]
Supply the key through ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the approved process environment. Never put it in a command or file.
Dry-run never reads that key. Apply reads it only for the selected operation.
The script sends the workspace header. The operator must verify key ownership and workspace authorization.
steps: Have the authorized administrator create and approve a dedicated non-default workspace.
Record its wrkspc_ identifier. Confirm its spend controls and intended data location.
Choose an approved, available Claude model. The script has no default model.
Use Python 3.9 or later. No third-party SDK dependency is required.
Inject the workspace-scoped key using the customer's approved secret-handling process.
items: API origin: https://api.anthropic.com
anthropic-version: 2023-06-01
anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01
anthropic-workspace-id: the explicit non-default workspace ID
No HTTP redirect following, automatic retries, custom endpoints, corporate tools, MCP servers, or uploaded files.
notes: The ID check validates syntax, not organization membership. The workspace-scoped key and provider authorization remain required.
A redacted plan is not evidence of successful authorization.
The current beta is enabled for API accounts according to Anthropic. Customer access still requires live validation. [V09]

sections.title: Create resources, then run separately
paragraphs: Every command defaults to dry-run and prints the intended JSON body with a redacted authentication header.
Add --apply only after reviewing that operation and approving cost.
Agent creation and environment creation are separate. Neither command starts a model turn.
The environment blocks outbound hosts and package-manager or MCP exceptions. The agent has no tools or skills. [V10, V11]
steps: Preview create-agent. Review the model, fixed system prompt, and empty tool lists.
Apply create-agent. Record the returned agent_id and version.
Preview and apply create-environment. Record environment_id.
Supply those exact IDs and version to run. Review the plan without Apply first.
Apply run to verify the lab environment and create one session. Inspect its pinned snapshot and synthetic user.message event.
Record session_id and event_id immediately. They support recovery and precise cleanup.
Observe end_turn_observed only after the corresponding user event, an agent message, and a successful idle stop reason.
items: The fixed prompt asks only: Synthetic lab: what is 2 + 2?
No command accepts arbitrary user prompts, files, MCP configuration, or corporate data.
Run refuses a resolved session with tools, skills, MCP servers, collaborators, or a different lab system prompt.
Before session creation, run verifies the environment ID, lab metadata, cloud type, blocked networking, and empty package lists. [V22]
Agent definitions are pinned by returned version. [V12, V13]
The session has a 50-cent list-cost budget. In-flight requests can exceed it. [V16]
HTTP event acceptance does not establish response completion. [V14, V15]
sections.code:
$WorkspaceId = 'RETURNED_NON_DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID'
$ModelId = 'APPROVED_CLAUDE_MODEL_ID'
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py create-agent --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --model $ModelId
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py create-agent --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --model $ModelId --apply
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py create-environment --workspace-id $WorkspaceId
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py create-environment --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --apply
$AgentId = 'RETURNED_AGENT_ID'
$AgentVersion = 1 # Replace with the returned version.
$EnvironmentId = 'RETURNED_ENVIRONMENT_ID'
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py run --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --agent-id $AgentId --agent-version $AgentVersion --environment-id $EnvironmentId
# Append --apply only after reviewing this exact run plan.
notes: The dry-run path placeholder {new_session_id} means the ID returned by session creation. It is not an API route.
The script replaces that placeholder only after receiving and validating the provider ID.
Polling allows 20 attempts by default, five pages per attempt, and a 120-second deadline. --max-polls accepts 1 through 60.
Each HTTPS operation also has a socket timeout and a one-megabyte response limit.
Timeouts stop local polling. They do not stop remote work or prove completion.
No model response text is printed, saved, forwarded, or submitted to another service.
The script reports event status and counts only. Verify answer quality manually in the approved provider interface.
Give the workspace ID to the Microsoft connection administrator. Enter its separate approved key directly in the wizard.

sections.title: Hand off for manual Microsoft preview connection
paragraphs: Use the platform onboarding chapter to connect Anthropic Claude Managed Agents. This is a preview connection. [V01]
ONB-07 is REQUIRED for agreed catalogue acceptance. Provider resource creation or a successful session does not prove registry synchronization.
Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and ordinary Messages API applications are not substitutes for Managed Agents.
steps: Confirm explicit approval for the Anthropic beta and Microsoft preview connection before proceeding.
Have the authorized administrator select Anthropic Claude Managed Agents in the Microsoft connection wizard.
Enter the approved non-default workspace ID and its separate workspace-scoped key directly in the wizard.
Validate and save the connection. Select Sync agents.
Record connection identity, workspace ID, synchronization status, timestamp, registry entry, and the matching provider agent_id as ONB-07 evidence.
Mark ONB-07 BLOCKED if beta or preview approval, access, or permissions prevent synchronization. This blocks agreed catalogue acceptance.
Keep required Claude ONB-07 and Bedrock ONB-10 evidence separate. Neither result substitutes for the other.
notes: Registry synchronization does not import all session transcripts or establish runtime telemetry.
Keep credentials out of screenshots and evidence files.

sections.title: Recover and remove exact resources
paragraphs: Do not rerun creation after an uncertain transport failure. It could create duplicate resources.
Use the printed session and event IDs to observe existing work without sending another prompt.
Delete sessions first. Delete the exact environment after its sessions are removed. [V17, V18]
Agent archive is irreversible. It prevents new sessions but does not stop existing sessions. [V19, V20]
steps: Preview watch, then add --apply to read the exact session's event history.
Preview delete-session for each recorded lab session. Apply only after confirming its ID.
Preview delete-environment for the recorded lab environment. Apply only after confirming its ID.
Preview archive-agent for the recorded lab agent. Apply only after approving irreversible archival.
Remove the Microsoft platform connection and have its credential owner revoke the dedicated workspace key.
items: Residual object: the archived agent definition remains. This demo does not claim permanent agent deletion.
No documented permanent agent DELETE endpoint was verified. None is invented.
Partial creation can leave an agent or environment when a later command fails. Keep every returned ID.
A failed run can leave an idle or active session. Review and delete that exact session separately.
A provider deletion error is a failed cleanup, not proof that the object is gone.
sections.code:
$SessionId = 'RETURNED_SESSION_ID'
$EventId = 'RETURNED_USER_MESSAGE_EVENT_ID'
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py watch --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --session-id $SessionId --event-id $EventId
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py delete-session --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --session-id $SessionId
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py delete-environment --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --environment-id $EnvironmentId
python .\providers\anthropic\managed_agent_demo.py archive-agent --workspace-id $WorkspaceId --agent-id $AgentId
# Each command above is dry-run. Add --apply separately after approving its exact target.
notes: Cleanup requires the same explicit workspace ID and an authorized workspace-scoped key.
API errors return a nonzero exit code. Response bodies are suppressed to avoid accidental credential disclosure.
Deleting the environment does not delete the agent definition.
No resources were created during local development or test execution.

chapters.title: OpenAI: no native Connected platforms demo
paragraphs: OpenAI is absent from Microsoft's supported Connected platforms list retrieved on September 18, 2026. [V01]
No native OpenAI connection procedure or registry connector is implemented here.
An OpenAI SDK runtime integration is a separate implementation. It does not establish a native registry-sync connector.

sections.title: Record the unsupported path accurately
paragraphs: Mark native OpenAI Connected platforms onboarding as unavailable in this source-verified scope.
Do not substitute Codex endpoint discovery, an Azure-hosted model, or mocked Microsoft APIs.
steps: Recheck the current Microsoft supported-platform list before a customer demonstration.
Use the separate SDK runtime chapter when an instrumented OpenAI-framework agent is required.
notes: This statement is date-bound. It is not a prediction about future connector support.
